newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen $0.50-$1.00 higher - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen $0.50-$1.00 higher - dealers.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices early Friday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher amid strong demand for hogs for a large weekend slaughter, livestock dealers said.
Trade estimates for Saturday slaughter range from 140,000 to 180,000 head, depending on how many hogs can be secured, they said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants were expected from $54.50 to $55.00 and Illinois top prices were seen at $55.00.
Indiana/Ohio buyers said top prices at the plant could range from $54.00 to $54.50.
Higher prices in the face of increased hog supplies has spurred talk that not only was retail demand heating up, but so must export sales.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota actual hog marketings Wednesday overran estimates by 9,000 head at 119,000, according to USDA. Thursday's estimate was 110,000 head, which some sources say would probably be exceeded again.
